approval_scope: Two presentation figures -- one policy degradation (C to F) and one policy upgrade (F to C), each in speed / gap / commanded-acceleration panels -- plus the six-transition and six-variant results table. Longitudinal only; no lateral movement, no third aircraft, no capacity result.

speed_envelope_mps.min_source: 1.2 x Vstall for a low-wing-loading eVTOL; below it the aircraft is no longer wing-borne
speed_envelope_mps.max_source: 156 kt, below the 170 kt maximum cruise reported for the Joby S4
speed_envelope_mps.note: sourced declared bounds, not calibrated capabilities of a specific airframe

headline_findings: The KS2 reference reaches all six policy targets exactly; the baseline ACC reaches none.
Opening: the baseline stops 100-135 m short while saturating its 2.0 m/s^2 braking limit; the shortfall does not grow with transition size.

Closing: the baseline shortfall equals the full transition (750, 1500, 2250 m) because its command is min(free-flow, following) and the free-flow term is exactly zero at cruise. Structural, not a gain-tuning question.
Effort runs opposite to achievement: the reference uses up to six times less peak acceleration and arrives.
The closing failure costs capacity rather than safety: an aircraft that cannot close its gap goes on holding up to 2250 m more separation than its policy requires.
excluded_from_approval: The leader-braking no-exit case is reported but is a diagnostic of a state with no longitudinal exit, not a controller-comparison result.
No string-stability, multi-aircraft, lateral or capacity claim is approved here.
